results.notes: All five Exp1 source workbooks use Sheet1; their SHA-256 hashes were verified against the supplied manifest. PT=1 is LLM partner (HAI), PT=0 is human partner (HH). TC=0 is the simple tire task and TC=1 is the complex VR task. The model workbook uses a trailing C for complex-task IDs; the rating workbooks use a leading (C). These labels were normalized before joining. The two task conditions contain distinct randomized people, not paired rounds. Both treatment task cells have 52 people and both control task cells have 50. The creativity-rating file has 1093 rated participant ideas with two observed ratings each. Its idea texts and participant IDs agree with the separate idea workbook. Empty spreadsheet rows are discarded. No participants, rated ideas, or ratings are excluded. The new outcome is the mean of the two ratings per idea, then the mean across each person's ideas, giving each person equal weight. All SDs use n-1. Computed values are in raw 1-5 creativity units; difference is treatment minus control. Its SE is the treatment coefficient's HC2 SE in OLS with an intercept and treatment indicator only. Randomization was individual, so no cluster or paired correction is used. There is no first-round result. Fixation averages rebuilt from the two expert ratings agree with model CF for every participant; 1415 partner-idea rows in that workbook carry no participant ratings and are excluded from the mediator audit. The five survey IS items average to model IS for the 202 participants with unambiguous survey IDs. The survey repeats (C)HH39 and omits (C)HH40; neither survey row is reassigned. The complete model table supplies IS=2.4 for HH39C and IS=2.0 for HH40C. This survey-label issue causes no exclusion from the model or ratings. The model C scores agree with independently rebuilt participant rating averages to floating-point precision. Main PDF p. 5 arm means, SDs, t and p reproduce at their printed precision; Table S5 (supplement PDF p. 10) supplies the group counts. The published t is human minus LLM, whereas the requested difference is LLM minus human. The paper does not identify the standardizer of its d or the estimand of its confidence interval; neither is used to calculate the new SE.

All five Exp2 source workbooks use Sheet1; their SHA-256 hashes were verified against the supplied manifest. NC=1 is constrained-responsive LLM (CAI), NC=0 is batch-responsive LLM (NAI). TC=0 is the simple tire task and TC=1 is the complex VR task. The model workbook uses a trailing C for complex-task IDs; the rating workbooks use a leading (C). These labels were normalized before joining. The two task conditions contain distinct randomized people, not paired rounds. Both treatment task cells have 52 people and both control task cells have 50. The creativity-rating file has 1204 rated participant ideas with two observed ratings each. Its idea texts and participant IDs agree with the separate idea workbook. Empty spreadsheet rows are discarded. No participants, rated ideas, or ratings are excluded. The new outcome is the mean of the two ratings per idea, then the mean across each person's ideas, giving each person equal weight. All SDs use n-1. Computed values are in raw 1-5 creativity units; difference is treatment minus control. Its SE is the treatment coefficient's HC2 SE in OLS with an intercept and treatment indicator only. Randomization was individual, so no cluster or paired correction is used. There is no first-round result. Fixation averages rebuilt from the two expert ratings agree with model CF for every participant; 1823 partner-idea rows in that workbook carry no participant ratings and are excluded from the mediator audit. The five survey IS items average to model IS for all 204 participants after normalizing full-width parentheses. Reproduction and new aggregation use explicitly distinguished sources: the published results reproduce from Exp2_model.xlsx C, but its NAI31C score is 2.07142857142857, while averaging both raters across that person's 14 ideas in Exp2_creativity_rating.xlsx gives 2.0357142857142856. Excel rows 449-461 have ratings (2,2), and row 462 has (3,2). All other 203 model C values agree with the rebuilt averages. The discrepancy is not resolved by changing any source or guessing a rating. The reproduced list uses the deposited model C that generated the paper; computed uses the explicitly requested average of the posted ratings. The author-model control mean is 2.30253968253968; the new control mean is lower by 1/2800. With author C, the sum-coded factorial ANOVA gives F=0.811027121759787, matching 0.811 (main PDF p. 6). Rebuilt ratings give F=0.82433513487643, which does not round to 0.811. The four printed cell means on main PDF p. 7 provide validation of task and treatment coding, not additional subgroup estimates. The pooled counts are printed in Table S6 (supplement PDF p. 11).

Supplement PDF p. 12, Table S7, Model 4 is reproduced as OLS of standardized C on the unchanged 0/1 treatment indicator and standardized CF and IS, with an intercept and no task term. Each continuous variable is centered and divided by its full-sample SD with n-1: SD(C)=0.464659021303457, SD(CF)=0.280232921637985, SD(IS)=1.16069229633898. This standardization is inferred from the joint reproduction of all three printed coefficients and model R2 and F; it is not explicitly documented in the paper. All 204 model rows have observed outcome, treatment and both mediators, so the complete-case model has 104 treatment and 100 control people. The experiment count checks compare to the demographic table, not a model-specific count printed in Model 4, which has no such count. The table calls its SE bootstrapped with 10,000 replications, but supplies no seed or resampling specification; that bootstrap SE is not claimed as reproduced. For orientation only, conventional OLS gives treatment SE=0.229646201146073, which rounds to the table's SE. The computed object reports the brief's unadjusted raw arm contrast and HC2 SE, not the mediator-adjusted direct coefficient; it intentionally shares the sample and computed values of the corresponding pooled record and is not independent evidence.
